newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair ready for direct China/Taiwan air links.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair ready for direct China/Taiwan air links.

text.p: Direct air links between China and Taiwan could happen at any time but would not have a big impact on Hong Kong Dragon Airlnnes (Dragonair), said Augustus Tang, its general manager of planning and international affairs.

The senior executive of Hong Kong's regional carrier was speaking to reporters the day after the first direct shipping link across the Taiwan Strait sailed into port. Industry observers said there is continuing speculation about the first direct air link starting. It is not a question of if but when, one aviation source said.

Tang said Dragonair is fully prepared for direct air links to start and when it does "it will happen very very fast. China is ready, it is the Taiwanese who are not. One of our key planning assumptions is that direct air links will start within the next three years."

Kaohsiung is Dragonair's busiest air route and a major cargo destination. Latest Civil Aviation Department statistic show that Taipei is Hong Kong's leading trading partner for both air cargo imports and exports during. During January, the port of Kaohsiung was the 12th biggest import port for Hong Kong goods and Dragonair carried about 1,200 tonnes during the month to and from Hong Kong.

"Direct air links won't have a big impact and we don't expect to lose business. Demand from China and Taiwan is expanding. We don't carry a huge amount of passengers from China, only about 15 per cent of them are from mainland China. When air links start, the market will become bigger. It will be a case of a smaller share of a bigger pie," Tang said.

Industry observers in the region said Macau's new airport stands to be hit hard by direct air links because it is heavily reliant on being used as a go-between offering 'semi-direct' flights between China and Taiwan with only the flight number being changed.
